source.text: Συμεὼν Πέτρος δοῦλος καὶ ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῖς ἰσότιμον ἡμῖν λαχοῦσιν πίστιν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Simeon Peter, slave and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those equal in honor with us having obtained faith in [the] righteousness of the God of us and Savior Jesus Christ:

en.L: Simeon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to those who have been allotted a faith equal in honor with ours, in [the] righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: From Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, to those who, through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, have received a faith that is worth just as much as our own.
en.R: This letter is from Simeon Peter. I am a servant of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and an apostle sent out by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I am writing to you who have been given faith, the same faith that we have and just as valuable. Our God and Savior, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, is righteous and fair, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given it to you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave it to us.

es.L: Simeón Pedro, esclavo y apóstol de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, a los que han recibido una fe de igual honor que la nuestra, en [la] justicia de nuestro Dios y Salvador {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: De Simeón Pedro, siervo y apóstol de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, a los que, por la justicia de nuestro Dios y Salvador {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, han recibido una fe tan valiosa como la nuestra.
es.R: Esta carta es de Simeón Pedro. Soy siervo de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y apóstol enviado por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} escribo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} recibido la fe: la misma fe que tenemos nosotros, y de igual valor. Nuestro Dios y Salvador, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, es justo e imparcial, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:se|os}} la ha dado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como nos la dio a nosotros.

sw.L: Simeoni Petro, mtumwa na mtume wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa wale waliogawiwa imani yenye heshima sawa na [ile] yetu, katika haki ya Mungu wetu na Mwokozi Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Simeoni Petro, mtumishi na mtume wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa wale ambao, kwa haki ya Mungu wetu na Mwokozi Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, wamepokea imani yenye thamani sawa na imani yetu.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Simeoni Petro. Mimi ni mtumishi wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na mtume aliyetumwa na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}. Ninawaandikia ninyi mliopewa imani, imani ile ile tuliyo nayo sisi, yenye thamani sawa. Mungu wetu na Mwokozi, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ni mwenye haki na hampendelei mtu. Amewapa ninyi imani hii kama alivyotupa sisi.

fr.L: Syméon Pierre, esclave et apôtre de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, à ceux qui ont reçu en partage une foi d’égale valeur à la nôtre, dans [la] justice de notre Dieu et Sauveur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: De la part de Syméon Pierre, serviteur et apôtre de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, à ceux qui, par la justice de notre Dieu et Sauveur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, ont reçu une foi qui a autant de valeur que la nôtre.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Syméon Pierre. Je suis serviteur de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, et apôtre envoyé par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. J’écris à vous qui avez reçu la foi, la même foi que nous, et qui a autant de valeur. Notre Dieu et Sauveur, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, est juste et équitable, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous l’a donnée comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous l’a donnée.

ko.L: 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 종이며 사도인 시므온 베드로가, 우리 하나님이시며 구주이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 의로 우리와 똑같이 귀한 믿음을 받은 사람들에게 [편지합니다].
ko.B: 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 종이며 사도인 시므온 베드로가, 우리 하나님이시며 구주이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 의로 우리와 똑같이 귀한 믿음을 받은 여러분에게 이 편지를 씁니다.
ko.R: 이 편지는 시므온 베드로가 보냅니다. 나는 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 종이며, 그분이 보내신 사도입니다. 나는 우리와 똑같은 믿음, 우리 믿음과 똑같이 귀한 믿음을 받은 여러분에게 이 편지를 씁니다. 우리 하나님이시며 구주이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 의로우시고 공정하셔서, 우리에게 주신 것처럼 여러분에게도 그 믿음을 주셨습니다.

vi.L: Si-mê-ôn Phi-e-rơ, nô lệ và sứ đồ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, gửi đến những người đã nhận được đức tin quý báu như của chúng tôi, trong sự công chính của Đức Chúa Trời và Cứu Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Si-mê-ôn Phi-e-rơ, đầy tớ và sứ đồ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, kính gửi những người đã nhận được một đức tin quý giá như đức tin của chúng tôi, nhờ sự công chính của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, là Đức Chúa Trời và Cứu Chúa của chúng ta.
vi.R: Thư này của Si-mê-ôn Phi-e-rơ. Tôi là đầy tớ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} và là sứ đồ được {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sai đi. Tôi viết cho anh chị em là những người đã được ban cho đức tin, cũng là đức tin mà chúng tôi có và quý giá như vậy. Đức Chúa Trời và Cứu Chúa của chúng ta, Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, là Đấng công chính và công bằng, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban đức tin ấy cho anh chị em như đã ban cho chúng tôi.

pt.L: Simão Pedro, escravo e apóstolo de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, aos que receberam por sorte uma fé de honra igual à nossa, na justiça do nosso Deus e Salvador Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: De Simão Pedro, servo e apóstolo de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, aos que, pela justiça do nosso Deus e Salvador Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, receberam uma fé que vale tanto quanto a nossa.
pt.R: Esta carta é de Simão Pedro. Sou servo de Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} e apóstolo enviado por {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Escrevo a vocês, que receberam a fé, a mesma fé que nós temos e de igual valor. O nosso Deus e Salvador, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, é justo e trata todos da mesma forma, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu essa fé a vocês como a deu a nós.

am.L: የኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ባሪያና ሐዋርያ [የሆነ] ስምዖን ጴጥሮስ፣ በአምላካችንና በአዳኛችን በኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ጽድቅ ከእኛ ጋር እኩል ክብር ያለው እምነት ለደረሳቸው፦
am.B: ከኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ባሪያና ሐዋርያ ከስምዖን ጴጥሮስ፣ በአምላካችንና በአዳኛችን በኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ጽድቅ የእኛን ያህል ዋጋ ያለው እምነት ለተቀበሉ።
am.R: ይህ ደብዳቤ ከስምዖን ጴጥሮስ ነው። እኔ የኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ባሪያ ነኝ፤ እርሱ የላከኝ ሐዋርያም ነኝ። የምጽፈው እምነት ለተሰጣችሁ ለእናንተ ነው፤ ይህ እምነት እኛ ያለን ያው እምነት ነው፤ ዋጋውም እኩል ነው። አምላካችንና አዳኛችን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ጻድቅና ፍትሐዊ ነው፤ ለእኛ እንደ ሰጠን ለእናንተም ሰጥቷችኋል።

decisions.choice: slave: someone owned by a master and wholly at his service
decisions.reason: δοῦλος is the ordinary word for a slave, someone who belongs to another, not a hired worker who could leave. Peter puts it before his title of apostle: he belongs to Jesus Christ before he speaks for him. In the Greek Old Testament the same word is an honored title for Moses and David as servants of the Lord (Joshua 14:7; 2 Samuel 7:5), so it carries both humility and honor, as in Philippians 1:1 and Jude 1.

decisions.choice: Simeon Peter: the apostle Simon, whom Jesus named Peter
decisions.reason: Συμεὼν is the Hebrew form of the name Simon. It is used of Peter elsewhere only in Acts 15:14, by James at the meeting in Jerusalem. Peter is the name Jesus gave him, meaning "rock" (John 1:42; Matthew 16:18). Some manuscripts have the more common form Simon here; the person is the same.

decisions.choice: our God and Savior Jesus Christ: one person, Jesus Christ, called both God and Savior
alternatives: two persons: "our God, and the Savior Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: One article, τοῦ, governs both nouns, θεοῦ and σωτῆρος, and one "our" stands with them. In Greek this usually means the two nouns name one person. The letter uses exactly the same pattern four times for "our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ" (1:11; 2:20; 3:2; 3:18), where no one doubts that one person is meant. Some read two persons here because the next verse distinguishes "God" and "Jesus our Lord" (1:2), and "Savior" is sometimes used of God the Father (Jude 25). But in 1:2 the two nouns have separate articles, and here they do not. Compare Titus 2:13 and John 20:28.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "our God and Savior"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts, Codex Sinaiticus among them, read κυρίου ("Lord") instead of θεοῦ ("God"), which makes the phrase match 1:11. That looks like a copyist bringing the verse into line with the familiar phrase. The great majority of manuscripts read "God". Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: those who have received a faith equal in honor with ours: believers given the same trust in Christ as the apostles
alternatives: the faith as a body of teaching
a faith equal to that of Jewish believers
decisions.reason: λαχοῦσιν means to receive something by lot or as a share, not to earn it: faith is God's gift. ἰσότιμον means equal in honor or value. "Ours" most likely means Peter and the other apostles who saw Jesus (1:16-18): those who believe later, without having seen, have a faith of the same worth (compare 1 Peter 1:8). Some take "us" as Jewish believers and the readers as Gentiles, but the letter says nothing else about that difference.

decisions.choice: righteousness: the fairness of God, who gives the same faith to all without favoring some
alternatives: the righteous standing God gives to believers
decisions.reason: δικαιοσύνῃ here belongs to God and Savior Jesus Christ and explains how the readers came to have a faith equal to the apostles': he treats all alike. In Paul the word often names the righteousness God gives (Romans 3:21-22), but here it describes God's own justice and fairness, as in Psalm 9:9. ἐν gives the means: "through" or "by" it.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: Our God and Savior, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, is righteous and fair, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given it to you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave it to us
alternatives: through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable turns the phrase into a sentence and says what righteousness means here (m6), and that the faith was given (m5). Both say a little more than the Greek, which only says the readers received their faith "in" his righteousness.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in Romans, "Jesus Christ" is the usual Spanish form of the name, "Jesucristo", by default; the alternative separates name and title, "Jesús, el Mesías". Where a comma must follow the alternative, it sits inside the span.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Peter writes to the churches in the plural throughout the letter. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). In this verse only Readable addresses the readers directly.

decisions.choice: Simeón Pedro
decisions.reason: The Greek has the Hebrew form of the name (meaning decision m2). Spanish keeps it as "Simeón", the form Acts 15:14 uses, rather than the familiar "Simón".

decisions.choice: siervo
decisions.reason: "Siervo" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "esclavo".

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, kwake)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb ("alivyotupa", "amewapa"), and a prefix cannot take a capital. So the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, and Swahili has fewer spans than English.

decisions.choice: Simeoni Petro
decisions.reason: The Greek has the Hebrew form of the name (m2). Swahili keeps it as "Simeoni" rather than the familiar "Simoni"; the person is the same.

decisions.choice: mtumishi
decisions.reason: "Mtumishi" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "mtumwa".

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: 2 Peter is a letter: Peter speaks to the readers about what God has given them and what they have heard, and French uses the passé composé for that. The examples from the past in chapter 2 are told the same way, as things the readers know ("Dieu n’a pas épargné les anges").

decisions.choice: Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (L), Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} (B, R); "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" with the article outside the span; the deity_pronoun span on every French pronoun for God or Christ, subject "il" included (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Peter, Hebrews and Colossians: "Jésus-Christ" is written without its hyphen so that both options read naturally, and since French must write the subject pronoun, "il" for God or Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does and also where French needs one the English lacks.

decisions.choice: esclave (L); serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the French style guide says for this word: Literal keeps "esclave", the person owned by a master (meaning decision m1), and Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Syméon Pierre
decisions.reason: The Greek has the Hebrew form of the name, Simeon, rather than the usual Simon (meaning decision m2). French keeps that difference with "Syméon", the form also used for Peter in Acts 15:14.

decisions.choice: the whole letter in 합쇼체 at every level, with "여러분" for the readers and "나" for Peter; no deity_pronoun spans (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean of 1 Peter, Colossians and Romans: the formal style of a letter read to the church. Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for God and Christ is carried by -시-, 께서 and "그분".

decisions.choice: "시므온 베드로"; "종" for the slave at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek has the Hebrew form of Simon's name (meaning decision); "시므온" is the established Protestant form of it (Acts 15:14). "종" as in the Korean of James and 1 Peter: it says that Peter belongs wholly to his master (meaning decision) without the picture of modern slavery.

decisions.choice: "우리 하나님이시며 구주이신 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as one person, Jesus Christ, called both God and Savior, and footnotes it. Korean "-이시며 ... -이신" joins both titles to the one name, where "과" (and) would suggest two persons. "구주" is the established word for Savior.

decisions.choice: "Si-mê-ôn Phi-e-rơ"; "nô lệ" (L), "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos; "tôi" and "anh chị em" through the letter, as in 1 Peter
decisions.reason: The Greek here has the Hebrew form of Peter's name, Simeon (m2), which Vietnamese gives in its Protestant form, as the English keeps "Simeon". "Nô lệ" and "đầy tớ" follow James 1:1 and the Vietnamese Romans; the forms of address follow 1 Peter.

decisions.choice: "Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, là Đức Chúa Trời và Cứu Chúa của chúng ta" (B)
alternatives: the Greek order, as at Literal
decisions.reason: One person is named both God and Savior (m3). In Vietnamese "Đức Chúa Trời và Cứu Chúa" before the name could be read as two persons, so Balanced puts the name first and gives both titles to it; Literal keeps the Greek order, as the English does. "Cứu Chúa" is the Protestant word for the Savior.

decisions.choice: Simão Pedro
decisions.reason: The Greek has the Hebrew form of the name (m2), which the English keeps as "Simeon". In Portuguese the apostle is known only as "Simão", and "Simeão" would make readers think of another man (the patriarch, or the old man in the temple, Luke 2:25). "Simão Pedro" names the same apostle; the meaning note keeps the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: capitalised pronouns, as the English setting offers
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change; pronouns for God and for Christ are written plainly through the letter.

decisions.choice: ባሪያ (slave) at every level, where the English Balanced and Readable say 'servant'
decisions.reason: The shared terms for the letters keep ባሪያ for 'slave of Christ' at every level, as Paul's letters do; in Amharic 'the slave of God' is an old title of honour, and the word keeps the sense of belonging wholly to a master (m1).

source.text: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πληθυνθείη ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Grace to you and peace may it be multiplied in [the] knowledge of the God and of Jesus the Lord of us.

en.L: Grace to you and peace be multiplied in [the] knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
en.B: May you have grace and peace in ever greater measure as you know God and Jesus our Lord.
en.R: I pray that you will have more and more grace and peace as you come to know God and Jesus our Lord better.

es.L: Gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y paz sean multiplicadas en [el] conocimiento de Dios y de Jesús nuestro Señor.
es.B: Que la gracia y la paz abunden cada vez más en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} al conocer a Dios y a Jesús nuestro Señor.
es.R: Pido a Dios que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} cada vez más gracia y paz, a medida que {{plural_you:conozcan|conozcáis}} mejor a Dios y a Jesús nuestro Señor.

sw.L: Neema kwenu na amani ziongezwe katika ujuzi wa Mungu na wa Yesu Bwana wetu.
sw.B: Neema na amani ziwe nanyi kwa wingi zaidi na zaidi katika ujuzi wenu wa Mungu na wa Yesu Bwana wetu.
sw.R: Ninaomba mpate neema na amani zaidi na zaidi, kadiri mnavyozidi kumjua Mungu na kumjua Yesu Bwana wetu.

fr.L: Que la grâce et la paix vous soient multipliées dans [la] connaissance de Dieu et de Jésus notre Seigneur.
fr.B: Que la grâce et la paix vous soient données avec une abondance toujours plus grande, à mesure que vous connaissez Dieu et Jésus notre Seigneur.
fr.R: Je prie pour que vous ayez toujours plus de grâce et de paix, à mesure que vous apprenez à mieux connaître Dieu et Jésus notre Seigneur.

ko.L: 하나님과 우리 주 예수를 아는 앎 안에서 은혜와 평안이 여러분에게 더욱 넘치기를 [빕니다].
ko.B: 여러분이 하나님과 우리 주 예수님을 알아 갈수록, 은혜와 평안이 여러분에게 더욱 풍성하기를 빕니다.
ko.R: 여러분이 하나님과 우리 주 예수님을 더 잘 알게 되면서, 은혜와 평안을 더욱더 많이 누리기를 기도합니다.

vi.L: Nguyện ân điển và bình an được gia tăng cho anh chị em trong sự hiểu biết Đức Chúa Trời và Đức Giê-xu, Chúa chúng ta.
