am.R: ከሄድኩ በኋላም እንኳ እነዚህን ነገሮች ሁልጊዜ ማስታወስ እንድትችሉ የተቻለኝን ሁሉ አደርጋለሁ።

decisions.choice: departure: death
decisions.reason: ἔξοδον means a going out, an exodus. It is used of death, and Luke 9:31 uses it at the transfiguration, where Moses and Elijah speak of Jesus' "departure" in Jerusalem. Peter goes on in the next verses to speak of that same mountain.

decisions.choice: I will make sure you can remember: by what he writes
alternatives: by arranging for a written account of Jesus, such as a Gospel
decisions.reason: Peter does not say how. The most natural reading is this letter itself, a written reminder that will last after he dies (1:12-13; 3:1). From early times some have connected the verse with the Gospel of Mark, which tradition links with Peter's preaching, but the text does not say so.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ σεσοφισμένοις μύθοις ἐξακολουθήσαντες ἐγνωρίσαμεν ὑμῖν τὴν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν, ἀλλ’ ἐπόπται γενηθέντες τῆς ἐκείνου μεγαλειότητος.

records.literal_gloss: Not for cleverly devised myths having followed we made known to you the of the Lord of us Jesus Christ power and coming, but eyewitnesses having become of the that one majesty.

en.L: For it was not by following cleverly invented myths that we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}; rather, we had become eyewitnesses of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty.
en.B: When we told you about the power of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming, we were not passing on clever stories that people had made up. We had seen {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness with our own eyes.
en.R: When we told you that our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is powerful and will come again, we were not repeating clever stories that someone had made up. We saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness for ourselves.

es.L: Porque no fue siguiendo mitos ingeniosamente inventados como {{plural_you:les|os}} dimos a conocer el poder y la venida de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, sino que habíamos llegado a ser testigos oculares de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} hablamos del poder de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} venida, no estábamos transmitiendo cuentos ingeniosos inventados por la gente. Habíamos visto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} grandeza con nuestros propios ojos.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} dijimos que nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} tiene poder y que volverá, no estábamos repitiendo cuentos ingeniosos que alguien había inventado. Nosotros mismos vimos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} grandeza.

sw.L: Kwa maana hatukuwajulisha nguvu na kuja kwa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa kufuata ngano zilizobuniwa kwa ustadi, bali tulikuwa tumekuwa mashahidi walioona kwa macho ukuu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Tulipowaambia habari za nguvu za Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} na kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, hatukuwa tukisimulia hadithi za ujanja zilizobuniwa na watu. Tuliuona ukuu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa macho yetu wenyewe.
sw.R: Tulipowaambia kwamba Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ana nguvu na kwamba atakuja tena, hatukuwa tukirudia hadithi za ujanja ambazo mtu fulani alizibuni. Sisi wenyewe tuliuona ukuu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

fr.L: Car ce n’est pas en suivant des mythes habilement inventés que nous vous avons fait connaître la puissance et la venue de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, mais nous étions devenus témoins oculaires de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} majesté.
fr.B: Quand nous vous avons parlé de la puissance de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} et de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} venue, nous ne transmettions pas des histoires habiles inventées par des gens. Nous avions vu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grandeur de nos propres yeux.
fr.R: Quand nous vous avons dit que notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est puissant et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} reviendra, nous ne répétions pas des histoires habiles que quelqu’un avait inventées. Nous avons vu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grandeur nous-mêmes.

ko.L: 우리가 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 능력과 오심을 여러분에게 알린 것은 교묘하게 꾸며 낸 신화를 따른 것이 아니라, 우리가 그분의 위엄을 직접 본 사람들이 되었기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 능력과 그분이 오실 것을 여러분에게 알렸을 때, 우리는 사람들이 교묘하게 지어낸 이야기를 전한 것이 아닙니다. 우리는 그분의 위엄을 우리 눈으로 직접 보았습니다.
ko.R: 우리가 여러분에게 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 능력이 있으시고 다시 오실 것이라고 말했을 때, 누군가가 꾸며 낸 그럴듯한 이야기를 전한 것이 아닙니다. 우리는 그분의 위대하심을 직접 보았습니다.

vi.L: Vì chúng tôi đã không theo những chuyện hoang đường được bịa đặt khéo léo mà cho anh chị em biết quyền năng và sự đến của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}; nhưng chúng tôi đã là những người chính mắt thấy sự uy nghiêm của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Khi chúng tôi nói với anh chị em về quyền năng của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} và sự đến của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, chúng tôi không truyền lại những chuyện khéo bịa đặt. Chính mắt chúng tôi đã thấy sự uy nghiêm của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Khi chúng tôi nói với anh chị em rằng Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} có quyền năng và sẽ trở lại, chúng tôi không kể lại những chuyện khéo léo do ai đó bịa ra. Chính chúng tôi đã thấy sự vĩ đại của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: Pois não foi seguindo mitos habilmente inventados que lhes fizemos conhecer o poder e a vinda do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}; ao contrário, tínhamos nos tornado testemunhas oculares da majestade {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.B: Quando falamos a vocês do poder do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} e da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} vinda, não estávamos repassando histórias engenhosas que alguém inventou. Nós vimos a grandeza {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} com os nossos próprios olhos.
pt.R: Quando dissemos a vocês que o nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} é poderoso e vai voltar, não estávamos repetindo histórias inteligentes que alguém inventou. Nós mesmos vimos a grandeza {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

am.L: የጌታችንን የኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ኃይልና መምጣት ያስታወቅናችሁ በብልሃት የተፈጠሩ ተረቶችን ተከትለን አይደለምና፤ ነገር ግን የእርሱን ግርማ የዓይን ምስክሮች ሆነን ነው።
am.B: ስለ ጌታችን ስለ ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ኃይልና ስለ መምጣቱ በነገርናችሁ ጊዜ ሰዎች የፈጠሯቸውን ብልሃተኛ ተረቶች አላስተላለፍንም። ግርማውን በገዛ ዓይናችን አይተናል።
am.R: ጌታችን ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ኃያል እንደ ሆነና ዳግመኛ እንደሚመጣ በነገርናችሁ ጊዜ አንድ ሰው የፈጠራቸውን ብልሃተኛ ታሪኮች እየደገምን አልነበረም። ታላቅነቱን እኛ ራሳችን አይተናል።

decisions.choice: cleverly invented myths: stories made up with skill to persuade
decisions.reason: μύθοις were stories of gods and heroes, and the word came to mean tales that are not true. σεσοφισμένοις means devised with cleverness. Peter may be answering a charge, since the false teachers mocked the promise of Christ's coming (3:3-4) and used "made-up words" themselves (2:3).

decisions.choice: power and coming: the coming of Christ in power, his return
alternatives: his first coming, when he lived on earth and showed his power
decisions.reason: παρουσίαν is the word the letter uses for Christ's future coming (3:4, 3:12; compare Matthew 24:27; 1 Thessalonians 4:15). The two nouns together likely mean his coming in power. The transfiguration (1:17-18) then shows in advance the glory in which he will come, as Jesus said just before it (Mark 9:1). Others take the coming as his life on earth, which the apostles saw for themselves.

decisions.choice: eyewitnesses of his majesty: those who saw his greatness for themselves
decisions.reason: ἐπόπται means one who watches, an onlooker. μεγαλειότητος is majesty, a greatness that belongs to God; Luke 9:43 uses it of "the majesty of God" just after the transfiguration. ἐκείνου ("that one") points strongly to Christ.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: clever stories that people had made up
decisions.reason: "Myths" today can mean ancient sacred stories without any claim about truth; Balanced and Readable say plainly what Peter means (m1).

decisions.choice: is powerful and will come again
decisions.reason: Readable follows m2 and says the coming is still to come; this is the uncertain point of that decision.

decisions.choice: ngano
decisions.reason: "Ngano" is a traditional tale or fable, the closest Swahili word for μύθοις. Balanced and Readable say "hadithi ... zilizobuniwa", made-up stories, as the English does (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: "신화" (L); "지어낸 이야기" (B, R); "오심" (L), "오실 것" (B, R) for his coming
decisions.reason: Myths are stories made up with skill to persuade (meaning decision). Literal keeps "신화"; Balanced and Readable say what they are. His coming is his return in power (meaning decision, footnoted), which Korean says with the verb and the honorific, as in James 5:7-8.

decisions.choice: exclusive "chúng tôi" for Peter and the other eyewitnesses (1:16-18)
decisions.reason: The "we" here is Peter with James and John, who were on the mountain, and does not include the readers, so Vietnamese uses the exclusive "chúng tôi", as the Vietnamese John does for its eyewitnesses (1:14).

decisions.choice: a vinda (L, B); vai voltar (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 3:4, 3:12): "vinda" is the word the other letters use for Christ's coming. "Parusia" is a technical term most readers do not know.

decisions.choice: መምጣት (coming) for the Lord's parousia, here and in 3:4 and 3:12
decisions.reason: As in 1 and 2 Thessalonians, the plain noun of 'to come' is kept for the parousia; ዳግም ምጽአት is a later church term, and 1 Peter's 'revealing' is a different Greek word, kept apart as መገለጥ.

source.text: λαβὼν γὰρ παρὰ θεοῦ πατρὸς τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν φωνῆς ἐνεχθείσης αὐτῷ τοιᾶσδε ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης· Ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός μου οὗτός ἐστιν, εἰς ὃν ἐγὼ εὐδόκησα καὶ ταύτην τὴν φωνὴν ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐνεχθεῖσαν σὺν αὐτῷ ὄντες ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ ὄρει.

records.literal_gloss: Having received for from God Father honor and glory, a voice having been borne to him such as this by the Majestic Glory: The Son of me, the beloved of me, this is, in whom I was well pleased \v 18 and this the voice we heard out of heaven borne, with him being on the holy mountain.

en.L: For [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] received from God [the] Father honor and glory when a voice such as this was borne to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by the Majestic Glory: "My Son, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} beloved, this is [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}], in whom I am well pleased" \v 18 and this voice we ourselves heard borne from heaven, being with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the holy mountain.
en.B: Honor and glory were given to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by God the Father, when these words came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the Majestic Glory: "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son; I take delight in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}." \v 18 We heard that voice ourselves as it came from heaven, while we were there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the holy mountain.
en.R: God the Father gave Jesus honor and glory. The voice of God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great glory came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son. I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}." \v 18 We heard that voice come from heaven ourselves, because we were there with Jesus on the holy mountain.

es.L: Porque [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}] recibió de Dios Padre honra y gloria cuando {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fue traída por la Gloria Majestuosa una voz como esta: «Mi Hijo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} amado, este es, en quien me complazco» \v 18 y esta voz la oímos nosotros mismos traída del cielo, estando con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en el monte santo.
es.B: Dios Padre {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio honra y gloria cuando desde la Gloria Majestuosa llegaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estas palabras: «Este es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo muy amado; en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me deleito». \v 18 Nosotros mismos oímos esa voz cuando vino del cielo, mientras estábamos con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en el monte santo.
es.R: Dios Padre dio a Jesús honra y gloria. La voz de Dios, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gran gloria, vino a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y dijo: «Este es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo. Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} amo, y estoy muy contento con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}». \v 18 Nosotros mismos oímos esa voz que venía del cielo, porque estábamos con Jesús en el monte santo.

sw.L: Kwa maana [{{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}] alipokea heshima na utukufu kutoka kwa Mungu Baba, sauti ya namna hii ilipoletwa {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} na Utukufu wenye Fahari: "Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, mpendwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, huyu ndiye, ambaye nimependezwa naye" \v 18 na sauti hii sisi wenyewe tuliisikia ikiletwa kutoka mbinguni, tukiwa pamoja naye juu ya mlima mtakatifu.
sw.B: Alipewa heshima na utukufu na Mungu Baba, maneno haya yalipomjia kutoka kwa Utukufu wenye Fahari: "Huyu ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ninayempenda sana; ninapendezwa naye kabisa." \v 18 Sisi wenyewe tuliisikia sauti hiyo ikija kutoka mbinguni, tulipokuwa pamoja naye juu ya mlima mtakatifu.
sw.R: Mungu Baba alimpa Yesu heshima na utukufu. Sauti ya Mungu, katika utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mkuu, ilimjia na kusema, "Huyu ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Ninampenda, na ninapendezwa naye sana." \v 18 Sisi wenyewe tuliisikia sauti hiyo ikitoka mbinguni, kwa sababu tulikuwa pamoja na Yesu juu ya mlima mtakatifu.

fr.L: Car [{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}] a reçu de Dieu [le] Père honneur et gloire, lorsqu’une voix telle que celle-ci {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a été adressée par la Gloire majestueuse : « Mon Fils, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} bien-aimé, c’est celui-ci, en qui j’ai pris plaisir » \v 18 et cette voix, nous l’avons entendue nous-mêmes, venant du ciel, quand nous étions avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sur la sainte montagne.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a reçu honneur et gloire de Dieu le Père, quand ces paroles {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sont venues de la Gloire majestueuse : « C’est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils bien-aimé ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait toute ma joie. » \v 18 Cette voix, nous l’avons entendue nous-mêmes venir du ciel, quand nous étions avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sur la sainte montagne.
fr.R: Dieu le Père a donné à Jésus l’honneur et la gloire. La voix de Dieu, dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grande gloire, est venue jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et a dit : « C’est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Fils. Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aime, et je suis très content de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. » \v 18 Nous avons entendu nous-mêmes cette voix venir du ciel, parce que nous étions là, avec Jésus, sur la sainte montagne.

ko.L: [그분은] 하나님 아버지께로부터 존귀와 영광을 받으셨습니다. 그때 장엄한 영광으로부터 이런 음성이 그분께 들려왔습니다. "이는 내 아들, 내 사랑하는 [아들]이다. 내가 그를 기뻐한다." \v 18 그리고 우리가 그분과 함께 거룩한 산에 있을 때에, 하늘에서 들려온 이 음성을 우리가 직접 들었습니다.
ko.B: 그분은 하나님 아버지께 존귀와 영광을 받으셨습니다. 그때 장엄한 영광 가운데서 그분께 이런 음성이 들려왔습니다. "이는 내가 사랑하는 아들이다. 나는 그를 기뻐한다." \v 18 우리는 거룩한 산에서 그분과 함께 있을 때에, 하늘에서 들려오는 그 음성을 직접 들었습니다.
ko.R: 하나님 아버지께서 예수님께 존귀와 영광을 주셨습니다. 크신 영광 가운데 계신 하나님의 음성이 그분께 들려왔습니다. "이는 내 아들이다. 나는 그를 사랑한다. 나는 그를 무척 기뻐한다." \v 18 우리가 거룩한 산에서 예수님과 함께 있었기 때문에, 하늘에서 들려오는 그 음성을 우리가 직접 들었습니다.

vi.L: Vì [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] đã nhận từ Đức Chúa Trời là Cha sự tôn trọng và vinh quang, khi có tiếng như thế này từ Đấng Vinh Quang Uy Nghiêm đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Đây là Con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Con yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đẹp lòng về Con" \v 18 và chính chúng tôi đã nghe tiếng ấy đến từ trời, khi chúng tôi ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên núi thánh.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời là Cha đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sự tôn trọng và vinh quang, khi có tiếng từ Đấng Vinh Quang Uy Nghiêm phán với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Đây là Con rất yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vui thích về Con." \v 18 Chính chúng tôi đã nghe tiếng ấy từ trời phán ra, khi chúng tôi ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên núi thánh.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời là Cha đã ban cho Đức Giê-xu sự tôn trọng và vinh quang. Tiếng của Đức Chúa Trời trong vinh quang lớn lao của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đến với Đức Giê-xu và phán: "Đây là Con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta yêu Con, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} rất hài lòng về Con." \v 18 Chính chúng tôi đã nghe tiếng ấy từ trời phán ra, vì lúc ấy chúng tôi đang ở với Đức Giê-xu trên núi thánh.

pt.L: Pois [{{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}] recebeu de Deus Pai honra e glória, quando uma voz como esta {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} foi trazida pela Glória Majestosa: "O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Filho, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} amado, este é [{{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}], em quem eu tenho prazer" \v 18 e esta voz nós mesmos ouvimos, trazida do céu, quando estávamos com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} no monte santo.
pt.B: Ele recebeu honra e glória de Deus Pai, quando da Glória Majestosa {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} veio esta voz: "Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Filho amado, que me dá grande alegria." \v 18 Nós mesmos ouvimos essa voz vindo do céu, quando estávamos com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} no monte santo.
pt.R: Deus Pai deu honra e glória a Jesus. A voz de Deus, na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} grande glória, veio até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e disse: "Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Filho, e eu {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} amo. Estou muito contente com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}." \v 18 Nós mesmos ouvimos essa voz vir do céu, porque estávamos lá com Jesus no monte santo.

am.L: [እርሱ] ከእግዚአብሔር አብ ሞገስንና ክብርን ተቀብሏልና፤ ከግርማዊው ክብር እንዲህ ያለ ድምፅ ወደ እርሱ በመጣ ጊዜ፦ «ልጄ፣ የምወደው ልጄ ይህ ነው፤ እኔ በእርሱ ደስ ብሎኛል» \v 18 ይህንም ከሰማይ የመጣውን ድምፅ እኛ ራሳችን ከእርሱ ጋር በቅዱሱ ተራራ ሳለን ሰማን።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር አብ ሞገስንና ክብርን ሰጠው፤ ይህም ከግርማዊው ክብር እንዲህ የሚል ቃል ወደ እርሱ በመጣ ጊዜ ነው፦ «ይህ የምወደው ልጄ ነው፤ በእርሱ ደስ ይለኛል።» \v 18 እኛም ከእርሱ ጋር በቅዱሱ ተራራ ላይ ሳለን ያን ድምፅ ከሰማይ ሲመጣ ራሳችን ሰማን።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር አብ ለኢየሱስ ሞገስንና ክብርን ሰጠው። በታላቅ ክብሩ ያለው የእግዚአብሔር ድምፅ ወደ እርሱ መጥቶ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህ ልጄ ነው። እወደዋለሁ፤ በእርሱም በጣም ደስ ይለኛል።» \v 18 ያ ድምፅ ከሰማይ ሲመጣ እኛ ራሳችን ሰማን፤ ምክንያቱም ከኢየሱስ ጋር በቅዱሱ ተራራ ላይ ነበርን።

decisions.choice: a sentence that breaks off: Christ received honor and glory, and we heard the voice
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with a participle, λαβὼν, "having received", but never reaches the main verb it expects. After the words from heaven Peter starts again: "and this voice we heard". The meaning is clear despite the break.

decisions.choice: the voice at the transfiguration
decisions.reason: Matthew 17:1-8, Mark 9:2-8 and Luke 9:28-36 tell how Jesus was changed before Peter, James and John on a mountain, and a voice from the cloud called him the Father's beloved Son. The same words were heard at his baptism (Mark 1:11). They echo Psalm 2:7, where God calls the king "my Son", and Isaiah 42:1, where God delights in his chosen servant.

decisions.choice: the Majestic Glory: God himself
decisions.reason: A reverent way of speaking of God without saying his name, in keeping with Jewish practice. In the Gospels the voice comes from the bright cloud (Matthew 17:5), the sign of God's presence (Exodus 40:34). Glory here is God's own presence and splendor.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "My Son, my beloved, this is"
alternatives: "This is my beloved Son", as in Matthew 17:5
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT follows an early manuscript reading with "my" twice and "this is" after the title. Most manuscripts have the order and wording of Matthew 17:5, which copyists knew well and are likely to have followed. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: we: Peter, with James and John, who were there
decisions.reason: ἡμεῖς is emphatic: "we ourselves". Only three disciples went up the mountain with Jesus (Mark 9:2). "The holy mountain" is holy because God was present there (compare Exodus 3:5); the Gospels do not name it.

decisions.choice: I am well pleased: I delight in him, and approve him
decisions.reason: εὐδόκησα is past in form but describes the Father's settled delight in his Son. It can also carry the sense of choosing, as in Isaiah 42:1.

decisions.choice: [he] received ... this is [he]
decisions.reason: Literal turns the opening participle into a verb with its subject supplied, and keeps the Greek break after the quotation (m1).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where the Greek says "him", since he was last named in verse 16.

decisions.choice: dearly loved; I take delight in him (B); I love him, and I am very pleased with him (R)
alternatives: beloved; in whom I am well pleased
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use current words for "beloved" and "well pleased" (m6).

decisions.choice: la Gloria Majestuosa
decisions.reason: The phrase is a reverent name for God (m3), so Spanish capitalises it as a title. "Majestuosa" keeps the link with "majestad" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: Utukufu wenye Fahari
decisions.reason: The phrase is a reverent name for God (m3), so Swahili capitalises it as a title; "wenye Fahari" (majestic) keeps the link with "ukuu" (majesty) in verse 16.

decisions.choice: Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}
decisions.reason: God the Father speaks, so his possessive takes the deity_pronoun span, as Jesus' own pronouns do in John. The fused form "Mwanangu" could not take the span. The fused "naye" (with him) is left plain, as a prefix is.

decisions.choice: la Gloire majestueuse
decisions.reason: A reverent way of naming God himself (meaning decision m3), with a capital as a title. "Majestueuse" keeps the link with "majesté" in 1:16, which comes from the same Greek root.

decisions.choice: the voice in the words of the Korean Matthew 17:5 and 3:17 at each level; "장엄한 영광" for God
decisions.reason: The voice at the transfiguration (meaning decision); the Korean is that of the Korean Gospels, in 해라체 as God speaks, so the reader hears the same words Peter heard. "장엄한 영광" is a title for God himself (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "[그분은] ... 받으셨습니다" as a full sentence (L, B, R)
alternatives: the broken sentence of the Greek
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence breaks off after "received honor and glory" (meaning decision). A Korean participle cannot hang unfinished in the same way, so every level completes it; the meaning decision tells the reader what the Greek does.

decisions.choice: "Ta" for God and "Con" for the Son in the voice from heaven, with the deity_pronoun span on "Ta" in mid-sentence
decisions.reason: God speaks of his Son, and Vietnamese lets the Father name him "Con" again rather than use a third-person pronoun, as the Vietnamese John does where the Father and the Son speak (17:1). God speaking says "Ta", as the style guide sets; "phán" is the verb for his voice.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Vinh Quang Uy Nghiêm" (L, B) for the Majestic Glory
decisions.reason: The Majestic Glory is God himself (m3), so Vietnamese writes it as a title, capitalised, with "Đấng"; Readable says that it was God's voice.

decisions.choice: O meu Filho, o meu amado, este é [ele], em quem eu tenho prazer (L); Este é o meu Filho amado, que me dá grande alegria (B); Este é o meu Filho, e eu o amo. Estou muito contente com ele (R)
alternatives: Este é o meu Filho amado, em quem me comprazo
decisions.reason: The voice at the transfiguration (m2), worded as in Matthew 17:5 and 3:17 so that the passages read alike. Literal follows this verse's own Greek order (m4), with "em quem eu tenho prazer" as in Matthew's Literal; Balanced and Readable use Matthew's words, without "Escutem-no", which this verse does not have.

decisions.choice: a Glória Majestosa
decisions.reason: A reverent name for God (m3), capitalised as a name; Readable says "a voz de Deus, na sua grande glória", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ልጄ (my Son) in the voice from heaven, with the wording of Matthew 17:5 at Balanced
decisions.reason: God speaks of 'my Son', as at the transfiguration in Matthew; ወልድ is kept for the absolute title beside the Father. Literal follows this letter's own order ('My Son, my beloved, this is', m4), which differs from Matthew's Greek.

source.text: καὶ ἔχομεν βεβαιότερον τὸν προφητικὸν λόγον, ᾧ καλῶς ποιεῖτε προσέχοντες ὡς λύχνῳ φαίνοντι ἐν αὐχμηρῷ τόπῳ, ἕως οὗ ἡμέρα διαυγάσῃ καὶ φωσφόρος ἀνατείλῃ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν· τοῦτο πρῶτον γινώσκοντες ὅτι πᾶσα προφητεία γραφῆς ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως οὐ γίνεται, οὐ γὰρ θελήματι ἀνθρώπου ἠνέχθη προφητεία ποτέ, ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου φερόμενοι ἐλάλησαν ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἄνθρωποι.

records.literal_gloss: And we have more firm the prophetic word, to which well you do paying attention as to a lamp shining in a murky place, until day dawns and morning star rises in the hearts of you, \v 20 this first knowing, that every prophecy of Scripture of own interpretation not comes about; \v 21 not for by will of man was borne prophecy ever, but by Spirit Holy being borne spoke from God men.

en.L: And we have the prophetic word [as] more firm, to which you do well to give heed, as to a lamp shining in a murky place, until day breaks and [the] morning star rises in your hearts, \v 20 knowing this first: that no prophecy of Scripture comes about from [one's] own interpretation; \v 21 for no prophecy was ever borne by [the] will of {{gender:a human being|man}}, but {{gender:people|men}}, borne along by [the] Holy Spirit, spoke from God.
en.B: So the message of the prophets is all the more certain for us. You are right to keep your eyes on it, like a lamp that shines in a murky place, until the day breaks and the morning star rises in your hearts. \v 20 Know this first and foremost: no prophecy in Scripture arises from anyone's own interpretation, \v 21 for no prophecy ever came because a human being willed it; rather, {{gender:people|men}} spoke from God as the Holy Spirit bore them along.
en.R: This makes us even more sure of what the prophets said. You are wise to pay close attention to their message. It is like a lamp shining in a dark and dirty place. Keep looking to it until day breaks and the morning star rises in your hearts. \v 20 Most important of all, you must understand this: No prophecy in Scripture came from the prophet's own ideas about what things meant. \v 21 Prophecy never came from what a person wanted to say. Instead, the Holy Spirit moved {{gender:people|men}}, and they spoke the words that came from God.

es.L: Y tenemos más firme la palabra profética, a la cual {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} bien en atender como a una lámpara que brilla en un lugar sombrío, hasta que despunte el día y el lucero del alba se levante en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones, \v 20 sabiendo esto primero: que ninguna profecía de [la] Escritura surge de interpretación propia; \v 21 porque nunca profecía alguna fue llevada por voluntad {{gender:de un ser humano|de hombre}}, sino que {{gender:personas llevadas|hombres llevados}} por [el] Espíritu Santo hablaron de parte de Dios.
es.B: Así, el mensaje de los profetas es aún más seguro para nosotros. {{plural_you:Hacen|Hacéis}} bien en fijar la mirada en él, como en una lámpara que brilla en un lugar sombrío, hasta que despunte el día y el lucero del alba se levante en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones. \v 20 {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}} esto ante todo: ninguna profecía de la Escritura surge de la interpretación propia de nadie, \v 21 porque ninguna profecía vino nunca porque un ser humano la quisiera; al contrario, hubo {{gender:personas|hombres}} que hablaron de parte de Dios mientras el Espíritu Santo {{gender:las|los}} llevaba.
es.R: Esto nos da aún más seguridad en lo que dijeron los profetas. {{plural_you:Hacen|Hacéis}} bien en prestar mucha atención a su mensaje. Es como una lámpara que brilla en un lugar oscuro y sucio. {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} mirándolo hasta que amanezca y el lucero del alba brille en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones. \v 20 Lo más importante de todo es que {{plural_you:entiendan|entendáis}} esto: ninguna profecía de la Escritura salió de las propias ideas del profeta sobre el significado de las cosas. \v 21 La profecía nunca vino de lo que una persona quería decir. Al contrario, el Espíritu Santo movió a {{gender:personas|hombres}} que hablaron las palabras que venían de Dios.

sw.L: Na tunalo neno la kinabii [kuwa] thabiti zaidi, nanyi mnatenda vizuri kulizingatia kama taa inayoangaza mahali pa giza na uchafu, mpaka siku ipambazuke na nyota ya alfajiri ichomoze ndani ya mioyo yenu, \v 20 mkitambua hili kwanza: kwamba kila unabii wa Maandiko hautokani na ufafanuzi wa [mtu] mwenyewe; \v 21 kwa maana hakuna wakati wowote unabii ulioletwa kwa matakwa ya binadamu, bali watu, wakibebwa na Roho Mtakatifu, walisema kutoka kwa Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ujumbe wa manabii ni wa hakika zaidi kwetu. Mnafanya vizuri kuukazia macho, kama taa inayoangaza mahali pa giza na uchafu, mpaka siku ipambazuke na nyota ya alfajiri ichomoze mioyoni mwenu. \v 20 Juu ya yote, fahamuni hili: hakuna unabii katika Maandiko unaotokana na ufafanuzi wa mtu mwenyewe, \v 21 kwa sababu hakuna unabii uliowahi kuja kwa sababu binadamu aliutaka; bali watu walisema kutoka kwa Mungu Roho Mtakatifu alipokuwa akiwabeba.
sw.R: Jambo hili linatufanya tuwe na uhakika zaidi juu ya yale ambayo manabii walisema. Ni busara kwenu kusikiliza kwa makini ujumbe wao. Ni kama taa inayoangaza mahali pa giza na uchafu. Endeleeni kuutazama mpaka kuche, na nyota ya alfajiri ichomoze mioyoni mwenu. \v 20 Jambo kuu kuliko yote, mnapaswa kuelewa hili: Hakuna unabii katika Maandiko uliotokana na mawazo ya nabii mwenyewe kuhusu maana ya mambo. \v 21 Unabii haukuja kamwe kutokana na kile ambacho mtu alitaka kusema. Badala yake, Roho Mtakatifu aliwaongoza watu, nao wakasema maneno yaliyotoka kwa Mungu.

fr.L: Et nous avons la parole prophétique [comme] plus ferme, à laquelle vous faites bien de prêter attention, comme à une lampe qui brille dans un lieu obscur, jusqu’à ce que le jour paraisse et que [l’]étoile du matin se lève dans vos cœurs, \v 20 sachant d’abord ceci : aucune prophétie de [l’]Écriture ne vient d’une interprétation personnelle ; \v 21 car aucune prophétie n’a jamais été apportée par [la] volonté d’{{gender:un être humain|un homme}}, mais c’est poussés par [l’]Esprit Saint que des {{gender:humains|hommes}} ont parlé de la part de Dieu.
fr.B: Ainsi le message des prophètes est d’autant plus sûr pour nous. Vous faites bien de garder les yeux fixés sur lui, comme sur une lampe qui brille dans un lieu sombre, jusqu’à ce que le jour commence à poindre et que l’étoile du matin se lève dans vos cœurs. \v 20 Sachez avant tout ceci : aucune prophétie de l’Écriture ne provient d’une interprétation personnelle, \v 21 car aucune prophétie n’est jamais venue de la volonté d’un être humain ; au contraire, c’est portés par l’Esprit Saint que des {{gender:humains|hommes}} ont parlé de la part de Dieu.
fr.R: Cela nous rend encore plus sûrs de ce que les prophètes ont dit. Vous avez raison de faire bien attention à leur message. Il est comme une lampe qui brille dans un endroit sombre et sale. Continuez à le regarder jusqu’à ce que le jour arrive et que l’étoile du matin se lève dans vos cœurs. \v 20 Le plus important, c’est que vous compreniez ceci : aucune prophétie de l’Écriture ne vient des propres idées du prophète sur le sens des choses. \v 21 La prophétie n’est jamais venue de ce qu’une personne voulait dire. Au contraire, l’Esprit Saint a poussé des {{gender:humains|hommes}}, et ils ont dit les paroles qui venaient de Dieu.

ko.L: 그리고 우리에게는 더욱 확실한 예언의 말씀이 있습니다. 여러분이 이 말씀에 주의를 기울이는 것은 잘하는 일입니다. 날이 밝아 샛별이 여러분의 마음속에 떠오를 때까지, 어두운 곳에 비치는 등불처럼 [그 말씀에 주의를 기울이십시오]. \v 20 먼저 이것을 아십시오. 성경의 모든 예언은 [예언자] 자신의 해석에서 나오지 않습니다. \v 21 예언은 결코 사람의 뜻으로 나온 것이 아니라, 사람들이 성령에 이끌려 하나님께로부터 [받아] 말한 것입니다.
ko.B: 그래서 우리에게는 예언자들의 말씀이 더욱 확실해졌습니다. 여러분은 날이 밝고 샛별이 여러분의 마음속에 떠오를 때까지, 어두운 곳에 비치는 등불을 바라보듯이 그 말씀에 주의를 기울이는 것이 좋습니다. \v 20 무엇보다 먼저 이것을 알아야 합니다. 성경의 어떤 예언도 누가 스스로 풀이해서 생긴 것이 아닙니다. \v 21 예언은 사람이 원해서 나온 적이 한 번도 없습니다. 사람들이 성령께 이끌려 하나님께로부터 받은 말씀을 전한 것입니다.
ko.R: 이 일로 우리는 예언자들이 한 말을 더욱 확신하게 되었습니다. 여러분은 그 말씀에 주의를 기울이는 것이 좋습니다. 그 말씀은 어둡고 더러운 곳을 비추는 등불과 같습니다. 날이 밝고 샛별이 여러분의 마음속에 떠오를 때까지 계속 그 말씀을 바라보십시오. \v 20 무엇보다 중요한 것은 이것입니다. 성경의 어떤 예언도 예언자가 자기 생각대로 일의 뜻을 풀이해서 나온 것이 아닙니다. \v 21 예언은 결코 사람이 말하고 싶은 것에서 나오지 않았습니다. 성령께서 사람들을 움직이셨고, 그들은 하나님께로부터 온 말씀을 전했습니다.

vi.L: Và chúng ta có lời tiên tri [như] càng vững chắc hơn, là lời anh chị em làm tốt khi chú ý đến, như đến ngọn đèn chiếu sáng trong nơi tối tăm, cho đến khi ban ngày ló dạng và sao mai mọc lên trong lòng anh chị em, \v 20 trước hết phải biết điều này: không có lời tiên tri nào trong Kinh Thánh đến từ sự giải thích riêng [của ai]; \v 21 vì không có lời tiên tri nào đã từng được đem đến bởi ý muốn của con người, nhưng con người, được Đức Thánh Linh dẫn dắt, đã nói từ Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Như vậy, sứ điệp của các nhà tiên tri càng được xác chứng chắc chắn hơn cho chúng ta. Anh chị em làm đúng khi chăm chú nhìn vào sứ điệp ấy, như nhìn vào ngọn đèn chiếu sáng trong nơi u tối, cho đến khi ban ngày ló dạng và sao mai mọc lên trong lòng anh chị em. \v 20 Trước hết, hãy biết điều này: không có lời tiên tri nào trong Kinh Thánh đến từ sự giải thích riêng của bất cứ ai, \v 21 vì không có lời tiên tri nào đã đến do ý muốn của con người; trái lại, con người đã nói từ Đức Chúa Trời khi được Đức Thánh Linh dẫn dắt.
vi.R: Điều này làm cho chúng ta càng tin chắc hơn những gì các nhà tiên tri đã nói. Anh chị em thật khôn ngoan khi chú ý kỹ đến sứ điệp của họ. Sứ điệp ấy giống như ngọn đèn chiếu sáng trong một nơi tối tăm và dơ bẩn. Hãy tiếp tục nhìn vào đó cho đến khi trời sáng và sao mai mọc lên trong lòng anh chị em. \v 20 Quan trọng hơn hết, anh chị em phải hiểu điều này: Không có lời tiên tri nào trong Kinh Thánh đến từ ý riêng của nhà tiên tri về ý nghĩa của sự việc. \v 21 Lời tiên tri không bao giờ đến từ điều một người muốn nói. Trái lại, Đức Thánh Linh đã thúc đẩy con người, và họ đã nói những lời đến từ Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: E temos ainda mais firme a palavra profética, à qual vocês fazem bem em prestar atenção, como a uma lâmpada que brilha em lugar sombrio, até que o dia amanheça e a estrela da manhã se levante nos corações de vocês, \v 20 sabendo primeiro isto: que nenhuma profecia da Escritura surge de interpretação própria; \v 21 pois nunca profecia alguma foi trazida {{gender:pela vontade de um ser humano|pela vontade do homem}}, mas, {{gender:levadas|levados}} pelo Espírito Santo, {{gender:pessoas|homens}} falaram da parte de Deus.
pt.B: Assim, a mensagem dos profetas é ainda mais certa para nós. Vocês fazem bem em manter os olhos nela, como numa lâmpada que brilha num lugar sombrio, até que o dia amanheça e a estrela da manhã se levante no coração de vocês. \v 20 Antes de tudo, saibam isto: nenhuma profecia das Escrituras nasce da interpretação pessoal de alguém, \v 21 pois nenhuma profecia jamais veio porque um ser humano quis; ao contrário, {{gender:pessoas|homens}} falaram da parte de Deus sob o impulso do Espírito Santo.
pt.R: Isso nos deixa ainda mais seguros do que os profetas disseram. Vocês fazem bem em prestar muita atenção à mensagem deles. Ela é como uma lâmpada que brilha num lugar escuro e sujo. Continuem olhando para ela até o dia amanhecer e a estrela da manhã nascer no coração de vocês. \v 20 Acima de tudo, vocês precisam entender isto: nenhuma profecia das Escrituras veio das ideias do próprio profeta sobre o significado das coisas. \v 21 A profecia nunca veio daquilo que uma pessoa quis dizer. Pelo contrário, o Espírito Santo moveu {{gender:pessoas, e elas|homens, e eles}} falaram as palavras que vinham de Deus.

am.L: ደግሞም ይበልጥ የጸና የትንቢት ቃል አለን፤ ቀን እስኪነጋና የአጥቢያ ኮከብ በልባችሁ እስኪወጣ ድረስ፣ በጨለማ ስፍራ እንደሚበራ መብራት እርሱን ብትከታተሉ መልካም ታደርጋላችሁ፤ \v 20 ይህን አስቀድማችሁ እያወቃችሁ፤ የመጽሐፍ ትንቢት ሁሉ ከራስ ትርጓሜ አይመጣም፤ \v 21 ትንቢት ከቶ በሰው ፈቃድ አልመጣምና፤ ነገር ግን ሰዎች በመንፈስ ቅዱስ ተነድተው ከእግዚአብሔር ተናገሩ።
am.B: ስለዚህ የነቢያት መልእክት ለእኛ ይበልጥ እርግጥ ሆኖልናል። ቀን እስኪነጋና የአጥቢያ ኮከብ በልባችሁ እስኪወጣ ድረስ በጨለማ ስፍራ እንደሚበራ መብራት ዓይናችሁን በእርሱ ላይ ብታደርጉ መልካም ታደርጋላችሁ። \v 20 ከሁሉ አስቀድሞ ይህን እወቁ፤ በመጽሐፍ ያለ ማንኛውም ትንቢት ከማንም ሰው የግል ትርጓሜ አይመነጭም፤ \v 21 ትንቢት ሰው ስለ ፈለገ ከቶ አልመጣምና፤ ይልቁንም ሰዎች መንፈስ ቅዱስ እየነዳቸው ከእግዚአብሔር ተናገሩ።
am.R: ይህም ነቢያት በተናገሩት ነገር ላይ ይበልጥ እርግጠኞች እንድንሆን ያደርገናል። መልእክታቸውን በጥንቃቄ ልብ ብትሉ ጥበበኞች ናችሁ። መልእክታቸው በጨለማና በቆሸሸ ስፍራ እንደሚበራ መብራት ነው። ቀን እስኪነጋና የአጥቢያ ኮከብ በልባችሁ እስኪወጣ ድረስ ወደ እርሱ መመልከታችሁን ቀጥሉ። \v 20 ከሁሉ በላይ ይህን ማስተዋል አለባችሁ፤ በመጽሐፍ ያለ ማንኛውም ትንቢት ነቢዩ ነገሮችን በራሱ ከተረዳበት መንገድ አልመጣም። \v 21 ትንቢት አንድ ሰው መናገር ከፈለገው ነገር ፈጽሞ አልመጣም። ይልቁንም መንፈስ ቅዱስ ሰዎችን አነሣሣ፤ እነርሱም ከእግዚአብሔር የመጣውን ቃል ተናገሩ።

decisions.choice: verses 19-21 are one sentence: "knowing this first" goes with "you do well to give heed"
alternatives: a new sentence at verse 20, as the SBLGNT punctuates it with a raised dot
decisions.reason: γινώσκοντες is a participle that agrees with "you" in ποιεῖτε: the readers do well to heed the prophetic word, knowing first where prophecy comes from. It has no verb of its own, so the record joins verses 19-21.

decisions.choice: we have the prophetic word made more sure: the transfiguration confirms what the prophets said
alternatives: we have something more sure than the voice we heard: the prophetic word itself
decisions.reason: βεβαιότερον is "more firm". Peter may mean that what the apostles saw on the mountain makes the prophets' word about Christ's coming all the more certain; or that Scripture is even surer than the experience he has just described. The "and" that links the verse to verses 16-18, and Peter's point that he is no teller of myths, favor the first. "We" may be the apostles, or Peter and his readers together.

decisions.choice: the prophetic word; prophecy of Scripture: the Old Testament Scriptures, above all what they promise about the coming of Christ
decisions.reason: προφητικὸν λόγον is the message of the prophets taken as a whole (compare 3:2, "the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets"). γραφῆς means Scripture.

decisions.choice: until the day dawns and the morning star rises: until Christ comes, and his light fills believers' hearts
alternatives: the inner light of growing understanding now, before he comes
decisions.reason: φωσφόρος means "light-bearer", the morning star that rises before sunrise. Numbers 24:17 speaks of a star coming out of Jacob, and Revelation 22:16 calls Jesus "the bright morning star". The day is the day of the Lord (3:10). Until then the prophetic word is a lamp in a dark place. Why the star rises "in your hearts" is less clear: it may be the full light believers receive at his coming, or the growing understanding they gain before it.

decisions.choice: murky: dark, dirty, gloomy
decisions.reason: αὐχμηρῷ means dry and dirty, and so dim and gloomy. The world before Christ's coming is such a place, and the prophetic word gives light in it.

decisions.choice: no prophecy arises from the prophet's own interpretation: prophecy did not begin in the prophet's own understanding
alternatives: no one may interpret prophecy by himself: the reader's private interpretation
decisions.reason: ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως is literally "of one's own interpretation" or "explanation", and the Greek does not say whose. Verse 21 begins "for" and speaks about where prophecy came from, not how it is read, which favors the prophet's own explanation: prophets did not make up what they said. Others take it as a warning to readers not to interpret Scripture for themselves, against the false teachers who twist it (3:16). Both readings agree that prophecy comes from God.

decisions.choice: borne by the Holy Spirit: carried along and moved by the Spirit
decisions.reason: The same verb, ἠνέχθη and φερόμενοι, is used for the voice "borne" from heaven in 1:17-18. Prophecy was never "borne" by human will; the prophets themselves were "borne along" by the Holy Spirit, as a ship is carried by the wind (Acts 27:15, 27:17 use the verb that way). They spoke, but what they spoke came from God.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "spoke from God"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "holy people of God" in place of "from God". The two readings differ only by a few letters in Greek. The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts with "from God". Reviewers must check the evidence against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}; {{gender:a human being|man}}
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings in general, as opposed to God; the prophets included women (2 Kings 22:14; Acts 21:9). The traditional forms remain as alternatives. Balanced and Readable say "a human being" and "a person" for the will.

decisions.choice: the message of the prophets is all the more certain for us (B); This makes us even more sure of what the prophets said (R)
alternatives: we have the prophetic word more sure
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow m2 and say what is more certain.

decisions.choice: the prophet's own ideas about what things meant
decisions.reason: Readable says whose interpretation is meant, following m6. That is the uncertain point of the verse; Literal and Balanced leave it open.

decisions.choice: the sentence is divided
decisions.reason: The Greek is one sentence (m1). Balanced and Readable break it into several English sentences and turn "knowing this first" into a command.

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas llevadas|hombres llevados}}; {{gender:las|los}}
decisions.reason: Spanish adjectives and pronouns agree with "personas" (feminine) or "hombres" (masculine), so the span takes in the participle (L) and the pronoun has its own span (B). Balanced says "un ser humano" for the will, as the English does, with no setting.

decisions.choice: el lucero del alba
decisions.reason: "Lucero del alba" is the everyday Spanish name for the morning star that rises before the sun, the "light-bearer" of the Greek (m4).

decisions.choice: binadamu; watu, no setting
decisions.reason: Swahili "binadamu", "mtu" and "watu" mean human beings, women and men, so the English gender setting has nothing to change; "wanaume" would mean males only.

decisions.choice: ulioletwa ... wakibebwa
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one verb for the voice "borne" from heaven (1:17-18), prophecy "borne" by human will, and the prophets "borne along" by the Spirit (m7). Swahili cannot use one verb for all three: "kuletwa" (brought) for the voice and for prophecy, "kubebwa" (carried) for the prophets.

decisions.choice: d’{{gender:un être humain|un homme}} (L); des {{gender:humains|hommes}} (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The words mean human beings (as the English span says). The default "humains" is inclusive and "hommes" the traditional alternative; "des" and "d’un" read correctly before both options.

decisions.choice: "샛별" for the morning star
decisions.reason: "샛별" is the plain Korean name for the morning star. The meaning decision reads its rising as Christ's coming and his light in believers' hearts, and footnotes the other readings; Korean keeps the picture at every level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "[예언자] 자신의 해석" (L); "누가 스스로 풀이해서" (B); "예언자가 자기 생각대로 ... 풀이해서" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads this as prophecy not beginning in the prophet's own understanding, and footnotes the reading that readers may not interpret it privately. Literal brackets the prophet as the English does; Balanced leaves the person open; Readable names the prophet, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "사람" and "사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The words mean human beings (the prophets of Israel); Korean "사람" includes men and women and has no generic masculine.

decisions.choice: "con người" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "con người" is a human being of either sex, so the gender setting has no second wording to offer. "Sao mai" is the morning star.

decisions.choice: {{gender:levadas|levados}} ... {{gender:pessoas|homens}} (L); {{gender:pessoas, e elas|homens, e eles}} (R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese participles and pronouns agree in gender with the noun, so the words that agree with "pessoas" or "homens" go under the same setting; each option then reads correctly. Balanced avoids the agreement with "sob o impulso do Espírito Santo".

decisions.choice: የአጥቢያ ኮከብ (the morning star)
decisions.reason: የአጥቢያ ኮከብ is the everyday Amharic name of the bright star seen before dawn, so the picture of m4 is plain at every level.
